locations.title: Times Square
locations.description: Neon canyon where Broadway meets the world.

locations.title: National September 11 Memorial & Museum
locations.description: Twin‑tower footprints re‑imagined as solemn waterfalls and an underground museum chronicling 9/11.

locations.title: Brooklyn Bridge
locations.description: 1883 engineering marvel linking boroughs by span.

locations.title: Central Park
locations.description: 843 acres of meadows, lakes, and woodland paths.

locations.title: Rockefeller Center
locations.description: Art Deco complex with Top of the Rock, skating rink, and public art.

locations.title: Empire State Building
locations.description: Art-Deco titan with 86th-floor observatory.

locations.title: The High Line
locations.description: Elevated rail line reborn as a linear park through Chelsea and Hudson Yards.

locations.title: Staten Island Ferry
locations.description: Free ferry offering spectacular views of the Statue of Liberty, Ellis Island, and Manhattan skyline—New York's best bargain sightseeing cruise.

locations.title: Statue of Liberty
locations.description: Copper colossus gifted by France in 1886.

locations.title: Eiffel Tower
locations.description: Wrought-iron lattice tower built 1887-89 for the 1889 Universal Exhibition; named after engineer Gustave Eiffel and now a 330-m-tall global icon.

locations.title: Notre‑Dame Cathedral
locations.description: Gothic masterpiece built from the 12th to 14th centuries with soaring flying buttresses and rose windows; seat of the Archdiocese of Paris.

locations.title: Pyramide du Louvre
locations.description: Glass pyramid designed by I.M. Pei and commissioned by President Francois Mitterrand; completed in 1989, it stands 22 m high with 673 panes and serves as the Louvre's main entrance.

locations.title: Arc de Triomphe
locations.description: Monumental arch at Place Charles de Gaulle honouring Napoleon's victories; construction began in 1806 and the 50-m-high arch is engraved with bas-reliefs and the names of battles and generals.

locations.title: Musee d'Orsay
locations.description: Former Beaux-Arts railway station turned museum housing world-famous Impressionist and Post-Impressionist paintings by Monet, Degas, Van Gogh and others.

locations.title: Palais Garnier
locations.description: Opulent 1,979-seat opera house completed in 1875 by architect Charles Garnier; its marble foyer and gilded auditorium epitomise Second-Empire grandeur.

locations.title: Pantheon
locations.description: Neoclassical mausoleum built between 1758 and 1790 as a church; it now honours France's great men and women, housing the tombs of Voltaire, Rousseau, Marie Curie and others.

locations.title: Place de la Concorde
locations.description: Vast 18th-century square designed by Ange-Jacques Gabriel and renamed during the French Revolution; features the 23-m Luxor Obelisk and two monumental fountains.

locations.title: Tuileries Garden
locations.description: Formal garden laid out by Catherine de Medicis in the 16th century and redesigned by Andre Le Notre for Louis XIV; it later became a stage for royal festivities and revolutionary events.

locations.title: Basílica de la Sagrada Família
locations.description: Gaudí's still‑unfinished basilica blending Gothic and Art Nouveau forms, begun in 1882 and expected to be completed in 2026.

locations.title: Park Güell
locations.description: Gaudí‑designed hillside park with mosaics and gingerbread gatehouses, built 1900–1914 and now a UNESCO site.

locations.title: Casa Batlló
locations.description: Gaudí's modernist house with skeletal balconies, a shimmering trencadís façade and a dragon‑like roof.

locations.title: Cathedral of Barcelona
locations.description: The 13th‑century Gothic cathedral of Saint Eulalia, crowned with gargoyles and a neo‑Gothic façade.

locations.title: Barri Gòtic
locations.description: Medieval core of Barcelona's old town—narrow alleys, hidden squares and centuries‑old buildings form a labyrinth of history.

locations.title: La Barceloneta
locations.description: Seaside quarter on a narrow peninsula known for its beach, seafood restaurants and lively boardwalk.

locations.title: Platja de la Barceloneta
locations.description: Barcelona's wide city beach with a lively promenade lined with restaurants and clubs.

locations.title: Arc de Triomf
locations.description: Red‑brick triumphal arch built as the gateway to Barcelona's 1888 Universal Exhibition.

locations.title: Santa Maria del Mar
locations.description: 14th‑century Gothic basilica in El Born, famed for its austere single‑style construction and widely regarded as Barcelona's most beautiful Gothic church.

locations.title: Palau de la Música Catalana
locations.description: Modernist concert hall and UNESCO site.

locations.title: Rijksmuseum
locations.description: Dutch national museum showcasing Golden Age masterpieces and Amsterdam's cultural heritage.

locations.title: Museumplein
locations.description: One of Amsterdam's largest public squares, lined by world‑class museums and wide green lawns.

locations.title: Anne Frank House
locations.description: Historic canal house where Anne Frank wrote her diary; now a museum of remembrance.

locations.title: Dam Square
locations.description: Amsterdam's central square — monuments, pigeons, and non‑stop city life.

locations.title: Royal Palace
locations.description: 17th‑century City Hall turned royal palace, presiding over Dam Square.

locations.title: Canal Ring
locations.description: UNESCO‑listed ring of 17th‑century canals defining Amsterdam's postcard views.

locations.title: Van Gogh Museum
locations.description: Home to the world's largest collection of Van Gogh paintings and letters.

locations.title: Jordaan
locations.description: Canal‑laced former working‑class district now famed for galleries and brown cafés.

locations.title: Albert Cuyp Market
locations.description: Bustling street market in De Pijp famed for its diverse food stalls and Dutch treats.

locations.title: Vondelpark
locations.description: Amsterdam's beloved 19th‑century park with lakes, lawns, statues and an open‑air theatre.

locations.title: Duomo di Milano
locations.description: Gothic cathedral begun in 1386, Italy's largest church, with thousands of spires and statues and the golden Madonnina atop its pink‑marble roof.

locations.title: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II
locations.description: 19th‑century glass‑roofed arcade linking Piazza del Duomo with Teatro alla Scala, built 1865‑1877 by Giuseppe Mengoni and named for Italy's first king.

locations.title: Castello Sforzesco
locations.description: 15th‑century Visconti–Sforza fortress turned ducal residence and barracks, now housing civic museums and artworks including Michelangelo's Pietà Rondanini.

locations.title: Teatro alla Scala
locations.description: Opera house opened in 1778 on the former site of Santa Maria alla Scala, designed by Giuseppe Piermarini and famed for premiering Italian operas.

locations.title: Basilica di Santa Maria delle Grazie
locations.description: Renaissance church and UNESCO site designed by Bramante and linked to Leonardo da Vinci's mural "The Last Supper".

locations.title: Navigli
locations.description: Romantic southwestern district defined by the Naviglio Grande and Naviglio Pavese canals—remnants of a 150‑km waterway system once used to transport goods and marble for the Duomo.

locations.title: Brera
locations.description: Bohemian–bourgeois quarter where cobbled lanes, cafés and art galleries attract artists and collectors around Palazzo Brera.

locations.title: Pinacoteca di Brera
locations.description: Milan's first public art museum at Palazzo Brera, showcasing prestigious masterpieces and sculptures from the Renaissance to the 20th century.

locations.title: Bosco Verticale
locations.description: Pair of residential towers completed in 2014 that host over 800 trees, 11,000 perennials and 5,000 shrubs—creating a vertical forest equivalent to a 20,000 m² woodland.

locations.title: Porta Nuova
locations.description: Contemporary business district around Piazza Gae Aulenti, part of Milan's urban regeneration and the first neighbourhood worldwide to earn both LEED and WELL certifications.

locations.title: Quattro Canti
locations.description: Baroque crossroads where Via Maqueda meets Corso Vittorio Emanuele; four concave facades symbolize the seasons and Palermo's historic quarters.

locations.title: Teatro Massimo
locations.description: Opera house inaugurated in 1897, renowned for grand neoclassical architecture, superb acoustics, and status as one of Europe's largest theaters.

locations.title: Palermo Cathedral
locations.description: Cathedral complex begun in 1185 that blends Norman, Gothic, Baroque, and Neoclassical styles; houses royal tombs and richly decorated chapels.

locations.title: Fontana Pretoria / Piazza Pretoria
locations.description: High-Renaissance fountain covering much of Piazza Pretoria; originally sculpted by Francesco Camilliani for a Tuscan villa, it features more than fifty statues of mythological figures whose nudity earned it the nickname Fountain of Shame.

locations.title: The Royal Palace (Palazzo dei Normanni)
locations.description: Europe's oldest royal residence, begun in the ninth century and expanded by Norman kings; today it houses the Sicilian Regional Assembly.

locations.title: Cappella Palatina
locations.description: Royal chapel commissioned by King Roger II and completed in 1143, famous for glittering Byzantine mosaics paired with carved Arab-Norman wooden ceilings.

locations.title: Ballarò Market
locations.description: Lively street market on Palermo's south side where vendors shout and scooters weave through stalls overflowing with produce, meats, and street food; the bazaar blends Italian staples with North African spices.

locations.title: Teatro Politeama
locations.description: Nineteenth-century neoclassical theater crowned with a bronze quadriga; its open-air stage and arcaded facade make it Palermo's second major opera house.

locations.title: La Martorana (Santa Maria dell'Ammiraglio)
locations.description: Twelfth-century church built by Admiral George of Antioch in thanks to the Virgin Mary; originally a Greek-cross plan, the church has been altered over centuries and even hosted Sicily's aristocratic parliament after the 1282 uprising.

locations.title: San Cataldo Church
locations.description: Arab-Norman church founded around 1160 by Maio of Bari; its austere interior was never decorated and it later served as a post office before restoration in 1885.
